skills.name: Discussing care for family members and friends

note.text: A discussion of care should ask what support a person wants instead of assuming every older person, child or disabled person has identical needs. Use polite offers, relevant questions and clear reasons. An offer is not permission to ignore a refusal. Language practice uses fictional cases; pupils do not need to disclose private health or family information. It does not train a learner to administer treatment or take over an adult’s medical responsibilities.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to offer and discuss respectful practical support without making assumptions about a person’s needs. Builds on: Form Three’s polite requests and reasoned suggestions. Leads to: family-life discussion and directed writing for an audience.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: A discussion of care should ask what support a person wants instead of assuming every older person, child or disabled person has identical needs. Use polite offers, relevant questions and clear reasons. An offer is not permission to ignore a refusal. Language practice uses fictional cases; pupils do not need to disclose private health or family information. It does not train a learner to administer treatment or take over an adult’s medical responsibilities.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original dialogue: Bih asks an imaginary older neighbour, Would you like help with this light bag? The neighbour accepts and says where it should go. Ayuk asks a friend what would make a group activity easier to join. If a younger sibling seems unwell, the fictional learner tells a responsible adult instead of inventing treatment.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Prepare short turns: state the point, give a relevant reason and invite a response. Use fictional people if the subject is private. Practise with a partner when available; written choices here do not establish oral fluency or listening ability. Challenge an idea without insulting the speaker.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: An offer means ignoring every refusal. Correction: The person should be able to accept or decline.
All support needs can be inferred from appearance alone. Correction: Ask about the particular need rather than assuming it.
Respect requires avoiding any practical question. Correction: A relevant question can be considerate and clear.
A dialogue authorises a child to prescribe treatment. Correction: Language practice does not supply clinical training or authority.
